descriptors.R: nominee of the party of the administration in office since 1969
descriptors.D: nominee of the party that held the presidency from 1961 to 1969 and holds majorities in both houses of Congress

compile_desc.R: the party of the administration in office since 1969
compile_desc.D: the party that held the presidency from 1961 to 1969 and holds majorities in both houses of Congress

others_line: Other candidates on some ballots, including an independent former senator and Libertarian and American Independent nominees (answer "other").
never_name: Ford, Carter, Mondale, Dole, Reagan, Nixon, McCarthy, Maddox, Rockefeller, Kissinger or Wallace

slice_sources.men: 1970 and 1980 censuses interpolated to November 1976; men who are citizens 18+ (Twenty-sixth Amendment) outside the eleven Southern states: white non-Hispanic US-born, naturalized citizens of any race, Black US-born, and US-born Hispanic, Asian, Native American and other; 50 states and DC; calibrated to certified 1976 returns.
slice_sources.women: 1970 and 1980 censuses interpolated to November 1976; women who are citizens 18+ (Twenty-sixth Amendment) outside the eleven Southern states: white non-Hispanic US-born, naturalized citizens of any race, Black US-born, and US-born Hispanic, Asian, Native American and other; 50 states and DC; calibrated to certified 1976 returns.
slice_sources.south-white: 1970 and 1980 censuses interpolated to November 1976; citizens 18+ in the eleven former Confederate states other than Black US-born (white non-Hispanic US-born, naturalized of any race, and US-born Hispanic, Asian, Native American and other); calibrated to certified 1976 returns.
slice_sources.black-south: 1970 and 1980 censuses interpolated to November 1976; Black US-born citizens 18+ in the eleven former Confederate states; Voting Rights Act coverage extended in 1975. Any shortfall against white turnout is counted as exclusion.
slice_sources.immigrants: 1970 and 1980 censuses interpolated to November 1976; noncitizen adults of any race, who could not vote in any state.

masks: the nominee of the party out of power
the President's rival for the nomination
